problem.title: A Non-Prime Card
problem.statement: One card is chosen at random from cards numbered 1 through 10. What is the probability that the chosen number is not prime?
hints: Subtract the probability of choosing one of those four cards from 1.

solutionSteps.title: Count the complement
solutionSteps.body: Four of the ten cards are prime: 2, 3, 5, and 7.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract from 1
solutionSteps.body: The probability of not prime is 1-4/10=6/10=3/5.

validationMethods: direct complement count: four prime cards among ten gives 1-4/10=3/5
notes: Recomputed answer: six of ten equally likely cards are non-prime, so the probability is 3/5.

problem.title: At Least One Tail
problem.statement: A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting at least one tail?
hints: At least one tail fails only when all three tosses are heads.
HHH is one of eight equally likely outcomes.

solutionSteps.title: Name the complement
solutionSteps.body: The complement of at least one tail is no tails, which is HHH.

validationMethods: independent exhaustive enumeration of eight coin strings, seven containing at least one T
notes: Recomputed answer: only HHH fails, leaving seven favorable outcomes among eight.

problem.title: Not Exactly One Head
problem.statement: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of not getting exactly one head?
hints: Exactly one head occurs in HT and TH.
Not exactly one includes both HH and TT.

solutionSteps.title: Measure exactly one
solutionSteps.body: HT and TH are two of the four equally likely outcomes, so P(exactly one head)=2/4.

solutionSteps.title: Check the language
solutionSteps.body: The complement contains HH and TT: two heads or no heads.

validationMethods: independent direct enumeration of favorable outcomes {HH,TT} gives 2/4=1/2
notes: Recomputed answer: HH and TT are the two not-exactly-one outcomes, giving 1/2.

problem.title: A Four in Three Spins
problem.statement: A fair spinner has four equal sections numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4. The spinner is spun three times. What is the probability that at least one spin lands on 4?
hints: The complement is no 4 on any spin.
There are three non-4 choices on each spin.

solutionSteps.title: Count all sequences
solutionSteps.body: There are 4^3=64 equally likely three-spin sequences.

solutionSteps.title: Count the complement
solutionSteps.body: No 4 leaves three choices on each spin, making 3^3=27 sequences.

validationMethods: independent binomial sum C(3,1)3^2+C(3,2)3+C(3,3)=27+9+1=37 favorable sequences
notes: Recomputed answer: 37 of 64 sequences contain one, two, or three occurrences of 4.

problem.title: At Least One Repeated Roll
problem.statement: A fair four-sided die numbered 1 through 4 is rolled three times. What is the probability that at least two of the rolls show the same number?
hints: The complement is that all three rolls are distinct.
For distinct rolls there are 4 choices, then 3, then 2.

solutionSteps.title: Count the whole
solutionSteps.body: There are 4^3=64 equally likely roll sequences.

solutionSteps.title: Count all-distinct sequences
solutionSteps.body: There are 4 choices for the first roll, 3 different choices for the second, and 2 unused choices for the third: 4·3·2=24.

validationMethods: independent favorable count: 4 all-equal sequences plus 4 choices for repeated value times 3 choices for distinct value times 3 positions, totaling 4+36=40
notes: Recomputed answer: 40 of 64 sequences contain a repeated value, so the probability is 5/8.
